p.title: Reactivity series

panels.t: Potassium (K) — reacts violently with cold water
Sodium (Na) — reacts violently with cold water; kept under kerosene
Calcium (Ca) — reacts less violently with cold water and starts to float
Magnesium (Mg) — reacts with hot water
Zinc (Zn) — reacts only with steam
Iron (Fe) — reacts only with steam
Copper (Cu) — no reaction with water

p.challenge: Put these metals in the order of the reactivity series, most reactive at the top.

p.title: Getting a metal from its ore

nodes.text: Ore is mined; gangue is removed
nodes.info: Gangue = unwanted earthy impurities.

nodes.text: Where is the metal in the reactivity series?
nodes.info: Its place decides the method.

nodes.text: High (Na, Mg, Ca, Al): electrolysis of the molten compound
nodes.info: Carbon cannot reduce these oxides.

nodes.text: Middle (Zn, Fe, Pb): roast sulphide ores or calcine carbonate ores
nodes.info: Roasting = heat strongly in excess air; calcination = heat in limited air. Both give the oxide.

nodes.text: Reduce the oxide with carbon
nodes.info: e.g. ZnO + C → Zn + CO.

nodes.text: Low (Hg, Cu): heat the ore in air
nodes.info: e.g. cinnabar (HgS) gives mercury.

nodes.text: Electrolytic refining
nodes.info: Impure metal = anode, thin pure strip = cathode; pure metal collects on the cathode and impurities settle as anode mud.

p.title: Diamond or graphite?
p.challenge: Both are pure carbon. Sort each property into the right allotrope.

items.text: Each carbon bonded to four others
items.why: Diamond: each C joins 4 others in a rigid 3-D network.
This rigid structure makes diamond very hard.
Diamond is the hardest natural substance.

items.text: Used in cutting and drilling tools
items.why: Its hardness makes diamond useful for cutting.

items.text: Each carbon bonded to three others
items.why: Graphite: each C joins 3 others in hexagonal layers.
The layers of graphite are slippery.

items.text: Used in pencils and as a lubricant
items.why: Its soft, slippery layers make it useful in pencils.

p.title: How soap cleans

nodes.text: Soap is added to the washing water
nodes.info: Soap = sodium or potassium salt of a long-chain carboxylic acid.

nodes.text: Is the water hard (Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ salts)?
nodes.info: Tube-well water is often hard.

nodes.text: Soap forms scum — little lather, soap is wasted
nodes.info: Scum is an insoluble, sticky precipitate.

nodes.text: Use a detergent instead
nodes.info: Its charged ends do not form insoluble precipitates with calcium and magnesium ions.

nodes.text: Micelles form around the oily dirt
nodes.info: Oil-loving tails point inward around the dirt; ionic heads face the water.

nodes.text: Rinse: the dirt is washed away
nodes.info: The micelles stay in the water and carry the dirt off.

p.title: Breaking down glucose

nodes.text: Glucose (6 carbons)
nodes.info: Food is broken down to release energy.

nodes.text: Broken into pyruvate (3 carbons) in the cytoplasm
nodes.info: This first step happens in every cell.

nodes.text: Is enough oxygen available?
nodes.info: During a hard 400 m race, muscles run short of oxygen.

nodes.text: In mitochondria: CO₂ + water + much more energy
nodes.info: Aerobic respiration; energy is stored as ATP.

nodes.text: In yeast or in our muscles?
nodes.info: Both can work without oxygen, but make different products.

nodes.text: Yeast: ethanol + CO₂ (fermentation)
nodes.info: Anaerobic respiration in yeast.

nodes.text: Muscles: lactic acid — causes cramps
nodes.info: Lactic acid builds up when oxygen runs short.

p.title: Double circulation

panels.t: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium
Right atrium → right ventricle
The right ventricle pumps it to the lungs to pick up oxygen
Oxygenated blood from the lungs enters the left atrium
Left atrium → left ventricle
The thick-walled left ventricle pumps it to the whole body

p.title: Insulin and blood sugar (feedback)

nodes.text: You eat sweets: blood sugar changes
nodes.info: The pancreas keeps checking the blood sugar level.

nodes.text: Has blood sugar gone up?
nodes.info: Pancreatic cells detect the level.

nodes.text: Pancreas releases MORE insulin
nodes.info: Insulin brings blood sugar down.

nodes.text: Pancreas releases LESS insulin
nodes.info: So blood sugar is not lowered further.

nodes.text: Blood sugar stays in the normal range
nodes.info: This is feedback control. Too little insulin causes diabetes.

p.title: Is the baby a girl or a boy?

nodes.text: Mother’s egg always carries an X
nodes.info: Females are XX, so every egg gets one X.

nodes.text: Father’s sperm: half carry X, half carry Y
nodes.info: Males are XY.

nodes.text: Which sperm fertilises the egg?
nodes.info: It is a matter of chance — 50% each.

nodes.text: X-sperm: XX → girl
nodes.info: The mother is not responsible for the sex of the child.

nodes.text: Y-sperm: XY → boy
nodes.info: The father’s chromosome decides.
